chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Yazid ibn Khalifah al-Harithi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man asked him (the Imam) while I was present, saying, 'I have a vineyard.' He said, 'Sell it as grapes.' The man said, 'But there are those who buy it [grapes] and make it into wine.' He said, 'Then sell it as juice.' The man said, 'He buys the juice from me and makes it into wine in my own skin flask.' He said, 'You sold it as permissible (halal), so he made it forbidden (haram); may Allah distance him [from good].' Then he paused for a moment, then said, 'Do not leave the price with him until it becomes wine, so that you take the price of the wine.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling grapes to someone who makes wine?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi illustrates the principle of 'sadd al-dhara'i' (blocking the means) in Shia jurisprudence, where the seller's knowledge of the buyer's intent to produce wine for consumption renders the transaction potentially impure or invalid. The Imam’s advice to withhold the price until the wine is actually produced ensures that the seller is not merely selling the raw material but is directly linked to the final prohibited product, thereby avoiding ambiguity (gharar) and ensuring the price reflects the 'wine' itself.
